questions.question:
When a system is taken from thermodynamic state i to f along the path iaf (see figure), it is found that the heat Q absorbed by the system is 50 cal and work W done by the system is equal to 20 cal. Along the path ibf Q = 36 cal. What is W along the path ibf ? (In cal.)
$ $
$ $
questions.explanation:
From the first law of thermodynamics
$ $ΔU = Uf – Ui = Q – W ...(i)
$ where$ Q is the heat absorbed by the system at W is the work done by the system.
$ For$ the path iaf; we have
$ Q$ = + 50 cal, W = +20 cal
$ $∴ ΔU = Q – W = 50 – 20 = 30 cal
$ Since$ internal energy of the system is a function of its thermodynamic state and depends only on temperature and no other factor. Therefore ΔU between i to f is always 30 cal whatever path be adopted.
$ For$ the path ibf,
$ Q$ = +36 cal and ΔU = 30 cal
$ $∴ W = Q – ΔU = 36 – 30 = 6 cal
$ $
